about: Shared test vectors of the settings-UI condition language (expr_version 1). The C++ reference (cpp/ui_expr_ref.h), the game evaluator and the launcher C# evaluator all read this one file and must give every answer written here; the meaning of every operator and function is in the header of cpp/ui_expr_ref.h. A context says what a case runs against: renderer, facts (the machine.json shape, plus live.*), config (the lines of larecomp.toml, typed or as text), and settings (the catalog slice with each setting's type, default and auto descriptor), defs and presets as in settings-ui.json; a context that lacks settings, defs or presets uses shared. ctx of a case is a name in contexts, or an inline context; a context may have a base (a name in contexts) and is then a JSON merge patch over it (RFC 7396: objects merge key by key, a null deletes the key, anything else replaces). Absent ctx is empty. expect null is the language null. cases are expressions. state_cases take a row of an example file and give the first state (or variant) whose when is true, with its enabled / label / suffix / tag; decode_cases the value a row decodes the settings to; listing_cases whether a row (hidden_unless) or a value (when) is listed; label_cases the label a value ends up with (its label_rules, first match wins). The example file also supplies settings, defs and presets for those four lists.

case_fields.ctx: a name in contexts, or an inline context (see about)
case_fields.expect: the value (true, false, null, a number, a text, a list); absent: only the other fields are checked
case_fields.syntax_error: true: the text must not parse (and then evaluates to null)
case_fields.unsupported_call: true: it parses but calls a function outside the v1 set (or with the wrong number of arguments): the whole expression is null
case_fields.paths: every path the text names, dotted, sorted, no duplicates
case_fields.unguarded_live: live.* paths that are not inside the left operand of a ??: lint 3 of the exporter
case_fields.cond: { matches, listed }: Matches(result) and ListedUnlessFalse(result), the way states / hidden_unless use the result
case_fields.state_cases: { id, file, row, [list: states | variants], ctx, expect: { state: index or null, enabled?, label?, suffix?, tag?, needs_restart? } }; no matching state: enabled true, the row's label, no suffix
case_fields.listing_cases: { id, file, ctx, expect_listed } plus row (its hidden_unless) or value (a value of the row, or of value_set, and its when)
case_fields.label_cases: { id, file, ctx, expect_label } plus row or value_set, and value

not := ! not | cmp, so this is !(1 == 1)

a number running into a word
